feat(update): every 30 minutes; auto-merge what lernapps update would have done

## Intent

Once an app is listed, each push to its main should lead to an update pull request by itself. When the checks pass and the change is no more than what lernapps update would have done, it should merge without a person. Until now the update ran once a day and auto-merged only new npm versions, so even a plain lernapps update needed a review.

## Key changes

- The update workflow runs every 30 minutes and by hand, for one app or all.
- It opens a pull request only once the app's own address serves the new commit, so the listing check sees the new version. Later pushes move the same pull request update/<id>; a pull request closed without merging stays closed; an unchanged branch is not pushed again.
- To classify an update, it checks out the listed commit, runs lernapps update on it with the tooling the new commit pins, and compares the result with the new commit. It auto-merges when nothing else differs beyond versions of existing npm dependencies and Markdown files outside src/ and public/. Everything else gets the label review.
- The pinned tooling must be a commit on main of lernapps/tooling.
- The classification runs without a secret; only opening the pull request uses the app's token.
- The plan records the decision.
